papers.title_in_file: UTILIZING SMALL QUANTUM COMPUTERS FOR MACHINE LEARNING AND GROUND STATE ENERGY APPROXIMATION
papers.version_note: arXiv:2403.14406v4, dated 20 September 2024. The file name carries an older title (Quantum Machine Learning With a Limited Number Of Qubits); the text is the paper the record names.
papers.what_it_is: A quantum circuit partitioning method that measures an observable on a large system through products of Pauli-string measurements on small subsystems, tested in simulation on a transverse-field Ising ground state and on a binary digit classification.

existing.note: The 100% out-of-sample figure holds only for the reduced-basis model (validation and testing). The full-basis model reached 98.9 on validation and 97.8 on testing. The authors also state that only one instance of each model was trained and that the results might be coincidental. The task ran on a simulation of an 8 qubit quantum computer, not on hardware.
existing.value: The authors report that the reduced-basis model reached 100.0 accuracy on validation and testing data for the classification of the digits 3 and 6, while the full-basis model reached 98.9 on validation and 97.8 on testing; the authors state that only one instance of each model was trained and that the results might be coincidental.
quotes: When applied to the classification between the digits 3 and 6, we were able to generalize to out-of-sample data with 100% accuracy.
However, only one instance of each model have been trained, so these results might be coincidental.
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, one training run per model, on a simulated device.
existing.reader_inference: The test set holds 91 samples, so 100.0 percent means all 91 were classified correctly in one run. The abstract's 100% does not say which of the two models it refers to.

existing.note: The Conclusion lists n = 2 among the tested sizes. Section 3.1.3, Section 4.1 and Table 1 list only n = 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16. The 0.1% figure is read from Figure 4 as an order of magnitude, and the results are simulations compared with exact diagonalization.

assertions.value: The authors describe quantum circuit partitioning as a hybrid quantum-classical approach in which a quantum computation is divided into smaller subsystems and the measurement results on these subsystems are combined using classical processing.
quotes: A quantum computation is divided into smaller subsystems and results of measurements on these subsystems are combined using classical processing.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the term it builds on (Abstract and Introduction).

assertions.value: The authors state that the expectation value on the full n-qubit system can be expressed in terms of products of measurements on the S subsystems, after the global unitary is written as a sum of Pauli strings.
quotes: system in Eq. 2 in terms of products of measurements on the S subsystems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation, but its statement and conditions could not be quoted whole because the text layer breaks the equations into single words.
assertions.reader_inference: The number of Pauli-string terms, not this identity, decides whether the method is efficient; the paper treats that next.

assertions.value: The authors state that the mitigation of the drawbacks of present methods comes at the cost of a limitation on the applicable quantum circuits.
quotes: However, the mitigation of these drawbacks does come at the cost of a limitation on the applicable quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Introduction states this limit of the method.

assertions.value: The authors state that, with one feature embedded per qubit, the qubit requirement scales linearly in the number of data set features, so an m-qubit computer with fewer qubits than features p requires the features to be divided into subsets of at most size m.
quotes: the qubit requirement scales linearly in the number of data set features p, thus limiting the data sets for which this can be done reliably.
If only an m < p-qubit quantum computer is available, we divide the features into S subsets of at most size m
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup for the supervised model.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for a linear combination of all possible n-qubit Pauli strings, the total number of expectation values can be made polynomial in the number of qubits n by partitioning the system into subsystems of a logarithmic number of qubits.
quotes: One can show that this number can be made polynomial in the number of qubits n.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation whose full statement could not be quoted because the text layer garbles the formulas.

assertions.value: The authors state that one coefficient is still required for every possible n-qubit combination of the Pauli-basis, so the number of coefficients scales as 4 to the power n (printed 4n in the text layer), and that this can be reduced by choosing a number of terms polynomial in n.
quotes: Despite the polynomial scaling of the number of expectation values, we still require one coefficient dp for every possible n-qubit combination of the Pauli-basis.
The scaling in the number of coefficients is hence 4n.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of the full construction in Section 2.2.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The polynomial route depends on a heuristic selection of terms by gradient or expectation magnitude; the paper gives no proof that the selected terms preserve model quality.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method needs the global unitary V to be unitary and that, since a general V is hard to construct efficiently, they restrict V to a product of factors, one per chosen Pauli-string, each built from a cosine and a sine of a real scalar.
quotes: In order to utilize our approach for methods such as the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), one is reliant on
the unitarity of the operator V .
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of the form of V it uses.
assertions.reader_inference: The restriction to this product form limits which ground states the ansatz can reach; the paper does not quantify that.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for K Pauli-strings of the chosen non-commuting construction per observable, the number of expectation values per observable is exponential in K (printed 22K in the text layer), which is constant in n for fixed K.
quotes: This results in 22K expectation values per observable Mm, and is thus constant in n for fixed K.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation whose construction conditions are only partly quotable from the text layer.
assertions.reader_inference: The count is exponential in K; it is constant only if K is held fixed as n grows.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the worst case a Hamiltonian with L terms needs S times L times an exponential in K number of expectation values (printed SL22K in the text layer), which can be made subexponential in n as long as L is subexponential in n.
quotes: This results in SL22K expectation values, which can be made subexponential in n as
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation whose full statement could not be quoted because the sentence continues on the next line of the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the variance derivation assumes each subsystem circuit resembles a unitary 2-design, and that the appendix derivation relies on the argument of McClean et al. that deep random circuits have the characteristics of 2-designs.
quotes: In [21], it is argued that deep random circuits have the characteristics of 2-designs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the assumption on which its barren plateau analysis rests (Section 2.4 and Appendix A).
assertions.reader_inference: The ansatzes used in the experiments are shallow circuits of two layers, so whether they resemble 2-designs is an assumption the paper does not test.

assertions.value: The authors state that terms of the observable which are local to a small subset of K of the subsystems can have the appropriate scaling for the variance of the gradients.

assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation under the 2-design assumption; the full statement could not be quoted because the text layer splits it across equations.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is an expected squared value under a 2-design assumption, not a measured variance of the full method.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for the VQE case with scalars drawn uniformly and K logarithmic in n, the worst case expectation of the squared coefficient magnitude scales polynomially in the number of qubits.
quotes: which scales polynomially in the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation whose formula could not be quoted because the text layer garbles it.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer shows the bound as one over a polynomial in n, so the term decreases polynomially; the sentence says only that it scales polynomially.

assertions.value: The authors state that the norm of the gradient for a single subsystem vanishes exponentially with the number of qubits in that subsystem, but vanishes polynomially with the total number of qubits if the subsystem qubit count is logarithmic relative to the total number of qubits.
quotes: but it vanishes polynomially with the total number of qubits if the subsystem
assertions.certainty_reason: An argument in the text, not a result with its conditions quoted whole.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total gradient is still exponentially vanishing, and that momentum-based gradient methods could help to escape the barren plateau.
quotes: Even though the total gradient is still exponentially vanishing, utilizing momentum-based gradient methods could then help to escape the barren plateau.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; no experiment in the paper tests momentum-based methods.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not show that the training method used in the experiments (Adam) escapes a barren plateau.

assertions.value: The authors state that their gradient estimation argument neglects the effect of accumulated errors from measurements on each subsystem, which could potentially impact the accuracy of the overall gradient estimate.
quotes: However, it should be noted that this reasoning neglects the effect of accumulated errors from measurements on each subsystem, which could potentially impact the accuracy of the overall gradient estimate.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit at the end of Section 2.4.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that the ground state energy approximation used gradient descent with the Adam optimizer, a learning rate of 0.1 and 200 training steps for every system, and compared the results with exact diagonalization of the Hamiltonian.
quotes: This is done with a learning rate of 0.1 and 200 training steps for every system.
The results are compared with the exact diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in Eq. 18, as shown in Fig. 4.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The values of the interaction strength J and the field strength h are not given in the text layer; the energies are in Figure 4, which the text layer does not carry.

assertions.value: The authors report that Figure 4 demonstrates the capability to approximate the ground state energy with a relative error within the order of 0.1% for all the tested numbers of qubits.
quotes: The results of Fig. 4 demonstrates the capability to approximate the ground state energy with a relative error within the order of 0.1% for all the tested numbers of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, from a figure the text layer does not carry.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is a single comparison with exact diagonalization per size, run in simulation, with no reported repeat over random initializations.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classification task was performed on a simulation of an 8 qubit quantum computer, on a binary task of the numbers 3 and 6, where each sample of the dataset is an 8 by 8 pixel image that would require a 64 qubit quantum computer to encode one pixel per qubit.
quotes: We will, similarly to [16], reduce this to a binary classification task of the numbers 3 and 6.
The task will be performed on a simulation of an 8 qubit quantum computer
Each sample is an 8 by 8 pixel image, which will require a 64 qubit quantum computer
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: No result in the paper was obtained on quantum hardware; every result is a simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total number of samples in the dataset is 364, divided into 182 samples for training, 91 samples for validation and 91 samples for testing.
quotes: The total number of samples in the dataset is 364, and these samples will be divided into 182 samples for training the model, 91 samples for validation and 91 samples for testing.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: A test set of 91 samples is small: one error changes accuracy by about one percentage point.

assertions.value: The authors report two model instances: a full-basis model with 240 trainable parameters, and a reduced-basis model with 156 trainable parameters, both trained for 400 epochs with the Adam optimizer at learning rate 0.1 and the mean squared error loss.
quotes: we have a total of 240 trainable parameters in this model.
This leads to a total of 156 trainable parameters.
the models were trained for 400 epochs using the Adam optimizer with learning rate 0.1.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 4.2 gives 56 expectation values and 112 coefficients for the full basis, but 28 expectation values and 28 coefficients for the reduced basis; Section 3.2.3 gives the coefficient count as equal to the measurement count. The counts do not follow one rule in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report, in the results table, accuracy and mean squared error for the full-basis and reduced-basis models: training 100.0 and 100.0 accuracy with 0.0090 and 0.0076 error, validation 98.9 and 100.0 accuracy with 0.0265 and 0.0171 error, and testing 97.8 and 100.0 accuracy with 0.0304 and 0.0250 error.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, one run per model.
assertions.reader_inference: The full-basis model has about 54 percent more trainable parameters than the reduced-basis model, yet scores lower on held-out data; with one run each, the difference is within what a single test error can cause.

assertions.value: The authors state that the final models were chosen from the epoch with the smallest mean squared error on the validation data, which was epoch 105 for the full-basis model and epoch 250 for the reduced-basis model, and that overfitting might be occurring at some state.
quotes: The final models were thus chosen from the epoch with the smallest MSE on the validation data.
For this case, the validation loss was minimized at epoch 105.
The validation loss was minimized at epoch 250.
suggesting that overfitting might be occuring at some state.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own model selection procedure.
assertions.reader_inference: Selection used the validation set; the testing set was applied only to the final models, so the testing figures are not selected on.

assertions.value: The authors state that the reduced-basis model generalizes to unseen data better than the full-basis model, suggest this might be due to the basis reduction acting as a form of regularization, and state that only one instance of each model was trained, so the results might be coincidental.
quotes: Interestingly, the model utilizing the reduced basis is generalizing to unseen data better than the model with the full basis.
This might be due to the basis reduction acting as a form of regularization, preventing overfitting.
However, only one instance of each model have been trained, so these results might be coincidental.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the single-instance limit in Section 4.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The regularization explanation is untested; the paper runs no repeat or ablation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the barren plateau experiment started with two subsystems of 8 qubits each and added subsystems of 8 qubits until 64 qubits, repeating 20 random parameter initializations and sampling the gradient with respect to the first parameter of the first subsystem.
quotes: we start out with two subsystems, each of 8 qubits, and successively add one and one subsystem of 8 qubits until we have 64 qubits.
This process is repeated for 20 random parameter initializations, where we sample the gradient with respect to the first parameter of the first subsystem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Twenty initializations and one gradient parameter is a small sample for a variance estimate.

assertions.value: The authors report from Figure 6 that, when measuring two-local Pauli-X strings between subsystems, the model does not suffer from exponentially vanishing gradients, and that they suspect the fluctuation in the variance is due to different parameter initializations.
quotes: We observe from Fig. 6 that when measuring two-local Pauli-X strings between subsystems, the model does not suffer from exponentially vanishing gradients.
We suspect that the fluctuation in the variance is due to different parameter initializations.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, from a figure the text layer does not carry, with 20 initializations per size.
assertions.reader_inference: The result holds for one measurement family (two-local Pauli-X strings between subsystems), not for an observable acting on all subsystems.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that their method evaluates expectation values of specific quantum states by decomposing the problem into smaller components for smaller quantum computers, can be tailored to mitigate barren plateaus, and applies to both ground state energy approximation and quantum machine learning.
quotes: In conclusion, our study presents an approach for evaluating the expectation values of specific quantum states by decomposing the problem into smaller components to be evaluated on smaller quantum computers.
The approach can be utilized in the context of ground state energy approximation and also for quantum machine learning
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's conclusion, supported by one Ising model family and one two-digit task in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that they would like to apply the method to diverse quantum systems and datasets to assess its generalizability.
quotes: Looking ahead, we would like to apply the method to diverse quantum systems and datasets to assess its generalizability.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Conclusion lists this as future work.
assertions.reader_inference: The tested scope is one Hamiltonian family and one binary digit pair.

assertions.value: The authors cite Bravyi et al. as showing that any (n + k)-qubit circuit in which each qubit participates in at most d two-qubit gates can be simulated on an n-qubit device with classical processing in 2 to the power O(kd) times a polynomial in n steps.
quotes: Bravyi et al. showed that any (n + k)-qubit circuit where each qubit participates in at most d two-qubit gates (d-sparse circuits), can be simulated on an n-qubit device with classical processing in 2O(kd)poly(n) steps [14].
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors cite earlier work as showing that, for a specific family of quantum circuits and observables, quantum circuit partitioning mitigates the problem of barren plateaus, but that the family does not allow observables that measure qubits in two partitions simultaneously.
quotes: For a specific family of quantum circuits and observables, QCP has also been shown to mitigate the problem of barren plateaus [17]
However, the specific family of quantum models they consider does not allow for observables that measure qubits in two partitions simultaneously.
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result attributed to other work.
